messages:
jordan: Heads-up: Cred-scan bot surfaced a leaked service token in archived logs for payments-proxy. Token looks like PAY-TOK-xx9f8e found in archives/2025/12/09/payments.log. Marking high severity.

cred-scan-bot: (automated) alert=leak_detected severity=high pattern=PAY-TOK-xx9f8e path=s3://redwood-archive/payments/2025/12/09/payments.log

tess: I'm on triage. Omar, can you confirm if token is live and where it's stored (Vault/Secrets manager)?

omar: Checking now. Token is referenced by payments-proxy config in older deploy (tag v0.9.1). Current live service uses short-lived OAuth, but archive had the old long-lived token. Also found a Vault entry at secret/data/services/payments with last_updated=2024-11-02.

lee: If it's in Vault kv v2 and archived copies exist in S3, our steps: 1) disable the leaked token immediately 2) rotate in Vault 3) re-encrypt with KMS 4) hunt for any CI artifacts + backups.

jordan: Can we do a quick check if the token was used recently? Omar, run CloudTrail / ingress logs query for that token string or corresponding service principal.

omar: Ran logs search — no recent inbound activity using that token within last 90 days. It likely fell out of use when we migrated to OAuth. Still treat as compromised.

tess: I'll open an incident P1 and notify partners. Assigning owners: Omar (rotation + vault), Lee (RBAC + audit), Jordan (forensics + comms).

jordan: Partner ops prefers we rotate and send new creds via their secure upload portal. We'll need to evidence rotation (audit IDs).

omar: Performing rotation. Steps: generate new token, write to Vault kv v2, push through KMS rewrap (AWS KMS example):
```bash
# generate new token (example)
NEW_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 24 | sed 's/^/PAY-TOK-/')
# write into Vault kv v2
vault kv put secret/services/payments token=$NEW_TOKEN owner=omar rotated_by=jordan rotated_at=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
# encrypt with KMS (aws kms encrypt)
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/redwood-partners --plaintext "$NEW_TOKEN" --output text --query CiphertextBlob | base64 --decode > payments_token.enc
```

lee: Before we finish rotation, lock down Vault read to a narrow group. I propose a temporary ACL that removes default-team read and only allows svc-payments role and security-admin. We'll apply for 4 hours.

omar: Creating a temporary policy 'payments-rotate' now and applying to the role used by the pipeline. Also creating a deny-list for old service accounts. Commands:
```bash
vault policy write payments-rotate - <<'HCL'
path "secret/data/services/payments" {
  capabilities = ["read", "update"]
}
path "secret/data/*" {
  capabilities = []
}
HCL
# bind to svc-payments
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/svc-payments policies=payments-rotate bound_service_account_names=svc-payments bound_service_account_namespaces=infra
```

cred-scan-bot: (automated) post-rotation scan report: initial_matches=1 post_rotation_matches=0 scanned_path=s3://redwood-archive/payments/2025/

jordan: Forensics note: archive copy shows token in plaintext in older log rotation job. We need to patch the log-rotator to scrub secrets before archival. Omar, please add a log-scrub step in the next PR and schedule backfill to remove tokens from archives.

omar: Will add scrubber: detect service token regex and replace with [REDACTED] before upload. Also kicking off an archive rewrite job to remove plaintext tokens from the last 3 years, starting with 2025 first.

lee: On audit logging: ensure Vault audit device is enabled and we export the specific request_id for the write event. Also capture KMS key version used to encrypt. Compliance will need these for proof.

omar: Vault audit enabled at /var/log/vault_audit.log — capturing entries now. Example (redacted): {"time":"2026-03-21T16:10:12Z","type":"create","path":"secret/data/services/payments","request_id":"r-55a1"}

jordan: KMS encrypt returned KeyId arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. Add that to the ticket.

tess: RBAC follow-up: we'll perform a narrow RBAC cleanup tomorrow to remove stale service accounts and group memberships. Lee, please prepare a list of candidates.

lee: Will do. Also question: should we rotate any downstream tokens that might have been created from that secret (e.g., webhook credentials)? I'm listing dependent services via config map scanning.

omar: Found two downstreams that pulled the secret into Docker image build args last year (billing-worker, invoice-archiver). I'm rotating those service tokens too and invalidating old images in the container registry.

cred-scan-bot: (automated) container-registry-scan: images_affected=2 tags=old-billing-2024-11,archiver-2024-10

jordan: CI artifacts: run a repo history scan for accidental commits and check GH actions logs. Use git-secrets and truffleHog for heuristics.

omar: Running quick git-secrets check on main branches; no matches. Will run truffleHog across historical commits in a scheduled job.

tess: Legal asked for timeline & impact. Jordan, please include detection time, archive path, rotation time, KMS key id, Vault request_id, and list of affected services.

jordan: Detection: 2026-03-21T16:05:00Z. Rotation complete: 2026-03-21T16:28:40Z. KMS KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. Vault request_id: r-55a1. Affected services: payments-proxy (archived), billing-worker, invoice-archiver.

lee: Post-incident actions: 1) require short-lived tokens for partner-facing secrets 2) add log-scrub to rotation jobs 3) add archive rewrite pipeline 4) RBAC cleanup 5) run scheduled git history scans. Assign owners and due dates in the incident ticket.

omar: I've uploaded the new token to the partner portal and confirmed acceptance. Also created PR for log scrubbing and started the archive rewrite job (tracking id JOB-4721).

cred-scan-bot: (automated) archive-rewrite job started id=JOB-4721 scope=2023-2025

tess: Great work everyone. I'm marking INCIDENT-2026-03-21-ARC as in containment. We'll run a 30-min postmortem tomorrow 10:00UTC to go over root cause and prevention.

jordan: Adding a proposal: move partner integrations to a short-lived signed token flow (10m TTL) via our auth-service; will draft RFC and post to eng-security later today.

lee: One last ask for SRE/oncall: add a preventive alert that flags any plaintext-looking token patterns in archive uploads before they're accepted. Oncall-sre, can you add?

oncall-sre: Yep, creating alert in Prometheus Alertmanager for uploads with regex match PAY-TOK-[a-z0-9]{6,}. Will set severity=critical and create a webhook to cred-scan-bot.

tess: Thanks team. Closing the loop for now; update incident ticket with any new findings. :white_check_mark:
